title: Order Numbers by Set Bits
statement:
You get an array nums of non-negative integers. Sort it by how many 1 bits each number has in binary, fewest first. Numbers with the same count of 1 bits go in ascending order of value.

Return the sorted array. Duplicates stay in the result as many times as they appear.

examples.why: Bit counts: 0 → 0, 8 (1000) → 1, 3 (11) and 5 (101) → 2, 7 (111) → 3. The 8 is big but has only one bit, so it comes early.
Every value has exactly two 1 bits, so the tie-break decides everything: plain ascending order.
1024 is a single bit, 1023 is ten 1 bits. Value order alone would put 1023 first.

hints: This is an ordinary sort with a custom order. What two things does the comparator compare, and in which order?
First the number of 1 bits, then the value itself. How do you count the 1 bits of a number?
x & (x − 1) clears the lowest 1 bit, so counting how many times you can do that before reaching 0 gives the bit count.

explain.intuition:
Sorting by two keys is the same as sorting a table by one column and breaking ties with another, like sorting files by type and then by name. Compare bit counts first; only when they are equal compare the values.

To count bits, the neat trick is x &= x − 1: subtracting 1 flips the lowest 1 bit to 0 and every 0 below it to 1, so the AND wipes exactly that one bit. The loop runs once per 1 bit. Since values here are at most 10 000, you can also pack both keys into one number, bits · 100 000 + value, and sort on that.
steps: Write bits(x): while x is not 0, do x &= x − 1 and count the steps.
Sort a copy of nums with a comparator: bits(a) − bits(b), and if that is 0, a − b.
pitfalls: Forgetting the tie-break, so numbers with the same bit count come out in input order.
Using JavaScript's default sort() for the tie-break. It compares numbers as strings, so 10 lands before 9.
Counting bits by converting to a binary string inside the comparator. It works but repeats the work O(n log n) times; precompute or use the bit trick.

solutions.title: Comparator with a bit counter
solutions.idea: Sort with a two-key comparator. The bit count clears the lowest set bit until nothing is left.

solutions.title: Pack both keys into one number
solutions.idea: Values are below 100 000, so bits · 100 000 + value orders by bit count first and value second.

followups: Values can now be up to 2³¹ − 1. Count bits in O(1) with a parallel bit trick.
Avoid comparison sorting: there are at most 14 different bit counts here. How would buckets help?
